have_skills: peripheral driver implementation from schematics/datasheets (PCB, EAGLE, Logic Analyzers, Oscilloscopes, ADXL345, TCA9548A, VL53L0X)
adjacent_skills: CPU/scheduling/timing optimization -> has CUDA kernel/memory-coalescing optimization experience, not RTOS-side latency/jitter tuning
software-in-the-loop simulation -> has CARLA robotics simulation, not firmware SIL specifically
distributed microcontroller network -> has multi-processor systems coursework, not a deployed multi-MCU aircraft network
production deployed embedded systems with long-tail edge cases -> has STM32/embedded capstone projects, not shipped production hardware
missing_skills: fault handling and recovery at the system level
platform-level interface design / reusable firmware components across subsystems
key_responsibilities: Design and build C++ firmware for a distributed system of aircraft microcontrollers
Develop reliable Ethernet, serial, and other microcontroller communication interfaces
Define platform-level interfaces and reusable firmware components
Own predictable/reliable performance across startup, real-time operation, fault handling, recovery
Optimize real-time behavior (CPU, memory, scheduling latency, jitter, resource contention)
Develop metrics, monitoring, troubleshooting for field deployment at scale
Develop Rust-based tooling and software-in-the-loop simulations

strengths: Peripheral driver implementation from schematics/datasheets is genuinely strong: TCA9548A I2C mux debugging, VL53L0X ToF and ADXL345 sensor integration, custom EAGLE PCB fabrication, and a bare-metal I2C driver written directly against GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 registers on STM32 (STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor).

Real interrupt-driven and basic RTOS work exists: FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination and interrupt-driven UART commands (Object Tracking Turret); timer-triggered ADC scans with interrupt-driven sample capture (STM32 Temp Monitor).
Serial protocol fluency (UART, I2C, SPI) is demonstrated across three separate projects, not just listed as a skill.

Systems debugging under integration pressure is shown concretely: resolved 11 distinct integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) in the COFFIN capstone, and root-caused sensor jitter via calibration in the gesture glove project.
real_gaps: Zero Rust exposure anywhere in the profile, and Rust tooling/SIL is an explicit JD deliverable.
No Ethernet experience as a firmware comms interface; all comms work is UART/I2C/SPI, which does not transfer directly.
No designed-in fault handling and recovery lifecycle (startup, fault, recovery) at a system level; the profile shows post-hoc debugging fixes, not fault-tolerant design.
No field-deployment metrics/monitoring/observability tooling; the closest analog (pynvml/psutil profiling) is model-inference profiling, not firmware production telemetry.
No platform-level interface design or reusable firmware components spanning multiple subsystems; every embedded project is a single- or dual-MCU standalone build, not a defined multi-node platform.

No true production/field-deployed system with long-tail edge-case hardening; everything is capstone, internship, or competition scope over a single semester, while the JD centers on a safety-critical aircraft system operating at global field sites.
overstated_by_keywords: "real-time firmware / RTOS" was counted as a full HAVE in the keyword pass, but on inspection it is basic FreeRTOS mutex usage in a hobbyist turret project, not the kind of real-time performance ownership (startup through fault recovery) the JD asks for on a safety-critical system.
understated_by_keywords: The keyword pass undersold how deep the hardware-to-firmware boundary work actually is: PCB fabrication in EAGLE plus multiplexer- and register-level driver debugging is unusually hands-on for this stage of a career and maps directly onto the JD's "fluency implementing peripheral drivers from schematics/datasheets" bullet.
screening_gaps: No production or shipped embedded system experience, while the JD explicitly asks for production experience on a real-world deployed, safety-critical system.
Zero Rust experience against an explicit Rust tooling requirement.
No Ethernet experience against an explicitly named comms interface.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The hardware-to-firmware boundary skills (peripheral drivers, PCB work, interrupt-driven serial comms, basic RTOS) are genuinely strong and specific, but the role's core is a production, safety-critical, multi-node aircraft platform with Rust tooling and Ethernet comms, and none of that has real backing in the profile. Worth a shot given the strong overlap on the hardware-debugging side, but the gaps are real, not just keyword noise.

outcome.notes: Form rejection (Embedded Firmware Engineer). No feedback.
